_about: AI music models the tool can use through fal.ai. 'verified' false = written from documentation,
run one cheap test before a big batch and fix the fields if fal.ai complains.
Prices are US dollars per minute of music, approximate; the ledger records what was really spent.
'max_seconds' is the longest single piece the model makes; longer tracks are made in pieces and joined.

ace-step.notes: Open-source model, cheap, makes up to 4 minutes in one go. Good for beats, lo-fi, EDM, pop instrumentals. '[inst]' in lyrics means instrumental. fal.ai calls the style words 'tags' (not 'prompt'); number_of_steps 60 is the model's maximum (its default is 27). Fields checked against fal.ai's published schema on 2026-10-15; still waiting for one real run to mark verified.

stable-audio.notes: Stability AI. Clean stereo, good for ambient, cinematic, sound beds. Short pieces only; the tool joins them.

lyria2.notes: Google's music model. Best sound quality for orchestral, jazz and acoustic. 30-second pieces, 48 kHz.

minimax-music.notes: Makes songs with a singing voice when you give lyrics. Good for Indian film-style songs. Write your own lyrics; never paste a real song's words. WARNING (schema check 2026-10-15): fal.ai's fal-ai/minimax-music takes 'prompt' = the lyrics and REQUIRES 'reference_audio_url', a real song with vocals to copy the style from. That breaks the rules at the top of README.md, so this model is not usable as written; use ace-step with lyrics instead until a lyrics-only endpoint is found.

elevenlabs-music.notes: ElevenLabs Music. Full tracks up to 5 minutes with proper structure. Dearest; use when one track must be perfect.
